settle_null_lost: the declarer took a trick, so the Null is lost
settle_enough: the declarer made {points} card points — 61 is enough
settle_short: the declarer made only {points} card points — short of 61
settle_schneider_missed: Schneider was announced, but the declarer made less than 90

advice_only_card: This is the only card you may play.
advice_draw_trumps_master: Draw trumps first: {card} is now the highest trump left, and leading it pulls the opponents' trumps out.
advice_draw_trumps_low: With many trumps, keep drawing them: a small trump lures out the opponents' high ones.
advice_cash_master_no_trumps: The opponents have no trumps left and {card} is the highest card of its suit — a sure trick.
advice_cash_master: {card} is the highest card of its suit. Take the trick while the opponents still have to follow.
advice_lead_low: Nothing wins for sure, so lead a small card worth nothing and keep your high cards.
advice_cannot_win: You can't win this trick, so throw off your least valuable card.
advice_last_win_plain: You play last: win with {card} and take the points along.
advice_last_no_points: This trick holds no points — not worth a trump.
advice_last_win_cheap_trump: You play last: the smallest trump that wins, {card}, takes these {pot} points.
advice_safe_win: Nobody after you can beat {card}. Win it with confidence.
advice_grab_pot: There are already {pot} points on the table — worth winning with a high card.
advice_second_low: Someone still plays after you. Play low and don't give your high cards away.
advice_def_cash_ace: Defenders take their aces early: play {card} and collect 11 points while the declarer still has to follow.
advice_def_no_trump_lead: Defenders don't lead trumps — that only draws them for the declarer. Lead a small side card.
advice_def_only_trumps: Only trumps left in your hand: play the smallest.
advice_def_smear: Your partner has this trick won — smear it: put {card} on it for {points} points.
advice_def_nothing_to_smear: Your partner has this trick won, but you have no points to add.
advice_def_overtake: The declarer is winning this trick. Beat the declarer with {card}.
advice_def_dont_feed: You can't beat the declarer, so give nothing away: play your smallest card.
advice_def_ace_before_declarer: The declarer still plays after you, but only a trump beats {card}. Worth a try.
advice_def_wait: The declarer hasn't played yet. Play low and see what comes.
advice_null_lead_declarer: In Null the declarer ducks: lead your smallest card and let someone else win.
advice_null_lead_defender: In Null the defenders try to force the declarer to win: lead low so there is nowhere lower to go.
advice_null_void_dump: You're out of this suit — the perfect moment to throw away your most dangerous high card.
advice_null_duck: Play the highest card that is still below the table, {card}: you duck this trick and get rid of a high card.
advice_null_forced: You can't duck any more. Play your smallest card and hope someone after you plays higher.
advice_null_def_under: The declarer is highest right now — play under with {card} and leave the trick with the declarer.
advice_null_def_dump: The declarer can no longer win this trick, so throw a high card away and keep your low ones to catch the declarer later.
advice_null_def_pressure: The declarer hasn't played yet. Play low and keep up the pressure.
drill_count_prompt: How many points is this trick worth?
drill_count_explain: {sum} = **{total}** points. Remember: A 11, 10 10, K 4, Q 3, J 2, everything else 0.
drill_count_hint: Add them one by one: A is 11, 10 is 10, K is 4, Q is 3, J is 2; 7, 8 and 9 count nothing.
drill_trumps_prompt: The game is **{contract}**. Tap every trump in this hand.
drill_trumps_explain_suit: The four Jacks are always trumps, plus every card of {suit}.
drill_trumps_explain_grand: In Grand only the four Jacks are trumps; all four suits are equal.
drill_trumps_hint_suit: Don't forget the Jacks — whatever suit is printed on them, they are trumps.
drill_order_prompt: The game is **{contract}**. Tap these cards from highest to lowest.
drill_order_explain_null: In Null the order is the "natural" one: {order}.
drill_order_explain: {order}. The Jacks come first, ranked ♣ ♠ ♥ ♦, then A, 10, K, Q, 9, 8, 7.
drill_order_hint_null: Null has no trumps; a Jack is an ordinary card: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7.
drill_order_hint: Think: the Jacks are highest (♣ ♠ ♥ ♦), then A, 10, K, Q, 9, 8, 7.
drill_legal_prompt: The game is **{contract}** and an opponent leads **{lead}**. Which of your cards may you play? Tap them all.
drill_legal_explain_any: You have no {led}, so any card is allowed.
drill_legal_explain_follow_trump: The lead is {led}, and if you have them you must follow. Jacks are trumps too: you may — and must — follow with them.
drill_legal_explain_follow_suit: The lead is {led}, and if you have that suit you must follow. A Jack is not part of the suit and cannot be used to follow.
drill_legal_hint: First ask: which suit does the lead count as? (Hint: {led}) Do you hold any of it?
drill_winner_why_top_trump: {card} is the highest trump in the trick.
drill_winner_why_only_trump: {card} is a trump, and a trump beats every side card.
drill_winner_why_suit: Nobody played a trump and {suit} was led, so {card}, the highest card of that suit, wins. Other suits don't count, however high.
drill_winner_prompt: The game is **{contract}**. The three cards were played from left to right. Which one wins the trick?
drill_winner_hint: First look for trumps. If there are none, only cards of the suit that was led can win.
drill_matador_prompt: The game is **{contract}**. How many matadors does this hand have?
drill_matador_explain_with: You hold ♣J, so you are "with". Count down from ♣J until the first trump you **don't** have: {n} in a row.
drill_matador_explain_without: You don't hold ♣J, so you are "without". Count down from ♣J the trumps you are **missing**, until the first one you have: {n} in a row.
drill_matador_hint: Look only at the top card, ♣J: holding it means "with", missing it means "without". Then count the unbroken run down ♣J ♠J ♥J ♦J A 10 K…
drill_value_prompt: You want to play **{contract}**. If you win, what is the game worth — in other words, how high can you bid?
drill_value_prompt_hand: You want to play **{contract}**, and as a **Hand** game (without looking at the skat). If you win, what is the game worth — in other words, how high can you bid?
drill_value_explain: {matadors}, game +1 → multiplier {mult}. The base value of {contract} is {base}, so {base} × {mult} = **{value}**.
drill_value_explain_hand: {matadors}, game +1, Hand +1 → multiplier {mult}. The base value of {contract} is {base}, so {base} × {mult} = **{value}**.
drill_value_hint: Game value = base value × multiplier. Multiplier = matadors + 1 (game) + any extras. Base values: ♦9 ♥10 ♠11 ♣12 Grand 24.
drill_settle_win_prompt: The declarer plays {name} with multiplier {mult} (game value {value}) and ends with **{pts}** card points. What does the declarer score?
drill_settle_lose_prompt: The declarer plays {name} with multiplier {mult} (game value {value}) and ends with only **{pts}** card points. What does the declarer score?
drill_settle_lose_tie: 60 is a tie, and a tie counts as a loss for the declarer.
drill_settle_schneider_prompt: The declarer plays {name}; before play the multiplier was {mult}. It goes very well: **{pts}** card points. What does the declarer score?
drill_settle_schneider_explain: {pts} ≥ 90 is **Schneider**, which adds 1 to the multiplier: {base} × {mult} = **+{score}**.
drill_settle_overbid_prompt: The declarer bid up to **{bid}** and plays {name}. After play it turns out the multiplier is only {mult} (game value {value}). The declarer took 70 card points. What is the score?
drill_settle_overbid_explain: A game value of {value} is below the bid of {bid}: that is an **overbid**, lost whatever the card points. It is scored at the smallest multiple that covers the bid, {base} × {mult} = {bid}, and doubled: **{score}**.
drill_settle_hint: First decide won or lost (61 card points; an overbid always loses). Won scores +game value, lost scores −2 × game value.

ex_play_illegal_jack: Remember: a Jack is a trump, not part of the suit printed on it.

skat_discard_prompt: The skat is in your hand now (12 cards). Tap two cards to put away — their points count for you.
play_lead_any: Your lead — any card is allowed.
play_tap: Tap a card to play it. Greyed-out cards can't be played now.
play_refusal: You must follow suit: the lead is **{led}**, and you still hold {led}, so you have to play {led}.
bid_hint_limit: This hand could play **{contract}**, worth **{limit}** as it stands — bid up to that and pass above it.
bid_hint_pass: This hand isn't strong enough. Pass and enjoy being a defender.
declare_prompt: Announce your game. You bid **{bid}**, so the game must be worth at least {bid}.
declare_covers: {contract}: worth {value} if you win, which covers your bid of {bid}.
declare_overbid: {contract} is worth only {value}, below your bid of {bid} — an overbid, lost however you play. Choose another game.
declare_hand_note: (Hand: a Jack in the skat can still change your matadors.)
result_early_claim_you: You claimed the rest: the last {n} tricks are yours.
result_early_claim_1: {name} claims the rest: the last {n} tricks are hers.
result_early_claim_2: {name} claims the rest: the last {n} tricks are his.
result_early_concede_you: {a} and {b} concede: your Null can't be beaten.
result_early_null_1: {name}'s Null can't be beaten any more – the game is decided.
result_early_null_2: {name}'s Null can't be beaten any more – the game is decided.
result_early_claim_named: {name} claims the rest and takes the last {n} tricks.
result_early_null_named: {name}'s Null can't be beaten any more – the game is decided.
result_early_null_you_named: Nobody can beat your Null any more – the game is decided.
result_line: {who}, playing **{contract}** with a bid of {bid}. Result: {reason}.
result_score_lost: Score for {name}: **{score}** (a lost game counts double)
result_score_lost_you: Your score: **{score}** (a lost game counts double)
skat_hint_pickup_covers: **Pick up the skat**: on average it improves a hand by about one card, and you get to put two useless cards away — Lina and Max always pick it up when they declare. Without the skat, this hand would be worth {value} as **{contract} Hand**, which covers your bid of {bid}; you can risk Hand (multiplier +1), but you will neither see the skat nor put anything away.
skat_hint_pickup_short: **Pick up the skat**: on average it improves a hand by about one card, and you get to put two useless cards away — Lina and Max always pick it up when they declare. Without the skat, the best this hand could play is {contract} Hand, worth {value} — below your bid of {bid}, so Hand now would be an overbid.
declare_hint_suit: Play **{contract}**: trumps in your hand (Jacks included): {trumps}; Aces in the side suits: {aces}.
declare_hint_grand: Play **{contract}**: Jacks in your hand: {jacks}; Aces: {aces}.
declare_hint_null: Play **{contract}**: every suit has a low card at the bottom and no high card can be forced to take a trick.
declare_hint_null_risky: Play **{contract}**: cards that could be forced to take a trick: {n} — every other game is less safe.
declare_hint_covers: Worth {value} if you win, which covers your bid of {bid}.
declare_hint_overbid: It is worth only {value}, below your bid of {bid} — no game covers it, so play the most promising one.
declare_hint_weak: This hand is not strong for any game, though: it is chosen only because its value covers the bid, and it will be hard to win — next time bid only as high as "How high can I bid?" says.
declare_hint_no_announce: Announce nothing: an announcement only wins if you fulfil it, and Lina and Max never announce either.

play_about_intro: Play Skat online against two AI opponents: free, with no sign-up, no registration and no ads. There is no download and no need to find a third player. The table opens directly in your browser. Bid, pick up the skat or play Hand, declare your game and play your ten cards.
play_about_title: A full game, one round at a time
play_about_text: The AI takes the other two seats. After the last trick, see the settlement and start another round. Suit games, Grand and Null are all part of the game. When you are unsure, ask for a hint at the table. Free play is separate from the daily leaderboard; reloading starts a new game.
game_learning_title: Learn Skat and look up the rules
game_learning_text: New to Skat? The free course takes you through the cards, trump order, bidding and scoring, step by step. Practise with cards and finish with a complete game. The Skat rules cover contracts, following suit, game values and examples you can return to while learning.
daily_static_lead: Free and without signing up. Everyone plays the same cards against the same AI opponents. New deals arrive at midnight in Berlin. After each deal, see how many points the AI scored in your seat.
daily_about_intro: In the daily Skat tournament you play {deals} deals against two AI opponents. Every participant receives the same cards and takes the same seat, so you can compare what you made of each hand. Continue your round on the same device; with an account, it belongs to your account. Each player has one round per day.
daily_scoring_text: Deals use Seeger-Fabian scoring and add up to your daily total. At the end, see your results and choose a nickname to appear on the leaderboard. For each completed deal, compare your score with the AI playing your seat. The leaderboard shows today and yesterday. A new tournament day begins at midnight in Berlin.
daily_play_description: Continue your tournament round for today. The cards, game state and result belong to your personal entry.
entry_new_text: {count} short interactive lessons take you from the 32 cards to a full game. You play real hands as you go, so there's no rulebook to memorize.
entry_game_text: Two AI players are ready any time, as often as you like. A live AI coach guides every move and answers your questions.
entry_friends_text: Open a private table and send the link. Your friends sit down without signing up – if someone is missing, the AI plays along.
entry_practice_text: Skat puzzles sorted by theme, from bidding to the last trick – like chess tactics puzzles.
faq_free_a: Yes. Every lesson and every game against the AI is free.
faq_account_a: No. You can learn and play without signing up, and your progress is saved in your browser. Signing in is optional.
faq_score_a: In free play, a won game scores its game value and a lost game costs twice its value. The daily tournament uses Seeger-Fabian: a won declarer game adds 50, a lost one costs another 50 on top of the doubled loss and gives each defender 40.
faq_rules_a: The international Skat rules (ISkO): bidding, suit games, Grand and Null, Hand, Schneider, Schwarz and Ouvert. Kontra/Re, Ramsch and Bock are not played. If everyone passes, free play deals again; in the tournament, the passed-in deal scores 0.
faq_phone_q: Can I play on my phone?
faq_phone_a: Yes. SkatGo runs in the browser on phones, tablets and computers, with nothing to install.

bidding_how_title: How to work out your bid
bidding_how_text: For suit games and Grand: **bid value = base value × multiplier**. The multiplier counts your matadors ("with" or "without" so many), plus 1 for "game" and 1 each for Hand, Schneider, Schneider announced, Schwarz, Schwarz announced and Ouvert. That takes a suit game to a multiplier of at most {suit}, and Grand to {grand}. Null is not multiplied; it has fixed values.
bidding_example_hand: **{game} Hand without {n}:** {n} matadors + 1 for game + 1 for Hand = multiplier {level}. {base} × {level} = **{value}**.

score_how: How to keep score: after each game, write the game and its value in the row. The declarer's column gets their new total: plus the game value when won, minus twice the value when lost. The defenders write nothing. At the end, settle up below by Seeger-Fabian.
